readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant repeat a water leak notification and keep the incident open until I inspect it, even if the sensor goes dry or loses contact?
directAnswer: Use a restored Toggle helper for the incident, one automation to record wet reports and one to repeat a phone message while the helper is on. Inspect the location, then use a reset script whose action-sequence condition requires the physical sensor to report off. Unknown/unavailable cannot clear it, but a stale off reading still requires human verification. Ordinary push is not a critical notification or guaranteed delivery; begin with the harmless helper-on rehearsal.
originalContribution: Sections 2-5 contain the complete helper, two-automation and guarded-reset walkthrough for one kitchen sensor. Section 6 rehearses the incident without wetting hardware. The six-row expected-behavior table separates currently wet, dry-but-uninspected, missing contact, restart and phone-delivery failures. An isolated Home Assistant 2026.9.4 run exercised 12 scenarios using the actual article YAML with simulated sensor/notify inputs and a 120-ms substitute for the five-minute wait. It verified startup/restore, reload, repeat, clear refusal and continued attempts after a handled send error; this is software validation, not a tested home.
limitations: No physical sensor, radio link, smartphone delivery, sound level, latency, plumbing device or real household was tested. The software test accelerated only the reminder wait and used isolated temporary state. A sensor can retain a stale off value; helper restoration after normal shutdown does not guarantee persistence after storage failure. Leaks entirely during downtime cannot be reconstructed. Startup/reload can resend immediately, reminders have no snooze, and the example controls no valve. The visible research-method note states documentation research and the limited software checks.
proofreadFixes: Corrected the draft’s old Developer tools navigation to current Settings > Tools, retaining an older-release note and administrator setup prerequisite. Kept exact raw wet/dry states distinct from unavailable/unknown, and explicitly identified stale off readings as a limit of the reset check. Made the no-snooze behavior and re-enable/Run actions recovery explicit. Clarified that startup/reload begins a fresh run rather than restoring elapsed wait time and can cause an extra message. Scoped continue_on_error to handled failures, distinguished ordinary push from iOS/Android critical settings, and linked Local Push prerequisites instead of implying Wi-Fi alone provides offline delivery. Added sideways-scroll cues for code/table on mobile. Final automated plain-English proofread PASS: four direct TLDR bullets, six ordered setup sections, clear reset rule, visible linked Tara Home byline, honest method note, original scenario table and professional source labels. Removed six incidental legacy-page whitespace changes from the required layout sync. All publishable changes are confined to this article and its required discovery files. Corrected the troubleshooting table so a manually set pending helper is not presented as proof that physical detection worked.

claimChecks.claim: Moisture binary sensors use on for wet and off for dry; unknown/unavailable are separate states. The reset sequence accepts only off; it does not prove that a stale value is fresh or that the leak was repaired.

A UI Toggle helper stores state and normally restores it after restart. A YAML initial:false override would discard the remembered incident; article does not promise recovery from a storage failure. Clean-restart restoration was also exercised with a synthetic helper in isolated HA 2026.9.4.
A state trigger with to:on and no from:off accepts reconnection into wet. The remember automation checks current sensor state inside its actions, and the isolated reconnect-to-wet scenario passed.
A Home Assistant start trigger provides an explicit check when the sensor or pending helper is already on; it cannot reconstruct events that ended while the server was stopped.
automation_reloaded is an official event. The two examples re-evaluate current state on it; they do not restore elapsed countdown time and may send an extra pending reminder.

Repeat-while checks the helper before each send. wait_template ends on a known-off helper or times out after five minutes; continue_on_timeout permits the next iteration. A handled notify failure can continue, but configuration and unhandled errors are not repaired. Accelerated runtime cases verified repetition, clear and handled-error continuation.
A false condition within the reset script sequence stops subsequent actions. The actual script refused wet, unknown and unavailable states in an isolated runtime; only off cleared the helper.
Restart mode stops an existing automation run before starting a new run. It does not provide exactly-once delivery or preserve a partially elapsed wait.
Phone notification setup requires a real registered notify.mobile_app action and permissions. Successful execution of a send action does not establish that a person received, heard or read it.

Ordinary pushes are not critical alerts. iOS critical sounds need the payload and permission; Android delivery priority and ttl are separate from alarm stream, channel and Do Not Disturb sound behavior.
Local Push uses a persistent direct connection with platform-specific prerequisites. Phone Wi-Fi connectivity alone does not prove a local notification path.
Current official action documentation names Settings > Tools > Actions; the article also identifies Developer tools as an older navigation label rather than assuming identical menus across releases.

Run actions does not exercise real trigger events; the helper rehearsal verifies the incident and reminder path only. Actual sensor detection and radio behavior need the exact manufacturer’s safe test procedure separately.
